hypothesis: The prior two-sided HAC classifier counts statistically significant negative slope as confirmed drift even though simulated positive-only hypothesis tests +0.0027/+0.005 vs 0. Direction-sensitive labels should reduce false confirmations.
scope: Positive-drift-or-no-drift synthetic hypothesis only; negative-slope evidence rejects the specified positive-drift hypothesis, not evidence that no negative drift exists.

frozen_rule.baseline: SG048 original pooled full240 HAC slope with z=2.291027529910169, plus its frozen warning-only boundary contradiction check
frozen_rule.slope_interval: Use SG048 pooled full-history HAC slope ±2.291027529910169*SE
frozen_rule.decision: If lower>0 -> positive drift confirmed; else if upper<0 -> negative direction detected, reject positive drift; else if entire interval within ±.0032 -> reject meaningful positive drift; otherwise unresolved
frozen_rule.boundary: Retain SG048 warning-only contradiction gate unchanged; if post-boundary primary and local diagnoses directly oppose one another, mark unresolved; never discard history

pilot.changes: Three false confirmations became correct rejections; no added false rejections or abstentions
pilot.disclosure: Evaluated before freeze; thresholds and label semantics frozen unchanged for holdout.

report: Paired SG048/SG049 correct FP FN abstain loss

All surviving errors and any new false negatives

limitations: This reinterprets the target hypothesis as positive drift; it cannot be applied unmodified to a generic bidirectional drift detector.
Nominal HAC intervals may under-cover in correlated regimes; directional semantics alone do not fix miscoverage.
